title: RWC25 FPRC Decision Qawe RSA
text:
FOUL PLAY REVIEW COMMITTEE
DECISION
PARTICULARS OF OFFENCE
Player’s surname Qawe Player’s Chumisa
forename(s)
Player’s Union South Africa
Match South Africa v France (Womens)
Competition RWC25 Match Date 7 September 2025
SELECT: Red card ☒ Citing ☐
Offence Breach of Law 9.13 – A player must not
tackle an opponent early, late or
dangerously. Dangerous tackling includes,
but is not limited to, tackling or attempting
to tackle an opponent above the line of the
shoulders even if the tackle starts below the
line of the shoulders.
Finding of Committee
Foul play determined? Foul Play Determined (plea of guilty)
Red Card Upheld
Red card upheld?
3 matches.
Summary of Sanction
In the event that the Player applies for and successfully completes World Rugby's Coaching
Intervention Programme, the sanction will be reduced by 1 match.
Fixtures to be confirmed.
Matches/tournaments
At a minimum to include Women's World Cup Quarter Final. It will also include the semi-final
included in sanction
should South Africa make it to that fixture (and the final in the event that the World Rugby
Coaching Intervention Program is not applied for and successfully completed by that time).
We are informed that the Player has no other confirmed fixtures beyond the tournament at
this stage. In those circumstances, in the event that South Africa is, for example, knocked out
of the tournament after the Quarter Final, the Player is to notify World Rugby of her playing
schedule as soon as it becomes available so that the FPRC can confirm the fixtures to be
included with the sanction.
REASONS FOR DECISION
• The Player was ordered off following receiving a red card during the fixture.
• The red card was issued for a breach of Law 9.13 – a player must not tackle an opponent early,
late or dangerously. Dangerous tackling includes, but is not limited to, tackling or attempting
to tackle an opponent above the line of the shoulders even if the tackle starts below the line of
the shoulders
• The referee's report is in these terms: "Dangerous tackle, direct contact to head, tackler
upright."
• The FPRO's report is in these terms: "Head contact, foul play, high degree of danger, no
mitigation."
• The video footage identifies an incident consistent with the above description.
Disciplinary Decision Foul Play Review Committee Page 1 of 3

• The medical evidence from France is that "Just spoke with our doctor. Our player is suffering of
an hematoma and bone contusion of the right zygomatic bone subject to clinical and
paraclinical evolution. We will see over the next few days what the outcome is."
The Player submitted that:
• the Player attempted a legitimate wrap tackle but failed to sufficiently lower her body height.
As a result, direct head contact occurred between her and France 11;
• the Player admits foul play, that there was head contact, that the degree of danger was high,
and that the incident warranted a red card;
• the Player's actions were not intentional (but were reckless);
• the Player attempted a legitimate wrap tackle but mistimed her body position;
• no provocation, retaliation or self-defence relevant;
• the victim player continued to play after the incident (and was still awaiting medical report);
• other players did not react as if it were an intentional incident;
• the victim player was not unusually vulnerable; and
• no premeditation.
The FPRC accepts these submissions.
Sanction
The FPRC determined the entry point as being mid-range given World Rugby's directive where there is
a head contact in a breach of 9.13.
The entry point for a mid-range for a dangerous tackle (9.13) is 6 weeks.
Having regard to a plea of guilty (at the first available opportunity), and that the FPRC was informed the
Player apologised to the victim player at the conclusion of the match, and feels remorseful for her
actions (which it accepts), the FPRC is of the view that a 50% reduction is appropriate mitigation in the
circumstances.
The FPRC notes in awarding the full 50% in mitigation that it considered the 2022 red card for a breach
of 9.13. However, there was no sanction imposed in that instance and, having reviewed the decision,
and given the effluxion of time, it believes 50% is the appropriate mitigation in present circumstances.
There were no aggravating circumstances identified by the FPRC.
Accordingly, the sanction proposed to be imposed by the FPRC (if accepted) is a sanction of 3 matches.
The Player has sought (and been granted) leave to apply to World Rugby 's Coaching Intervention
Program. In the event that the Player applies for and successfully completes the Program, the sanction
would be reduced by 1 match.
Disciplinary Decision Foul Play Review Committee Page 2 of 3

At a minimum the Player's sanction will include Women's World Cup Quarter Final. It will also include
the semi-final should South Africa make it to that fixture (and the final in the event that the World
Rugby Coaching Intervention Program is not applied for and successfully completed by that time).
We are informed that the Player has no other confirmed fixtures beyond the tournament at this stage.
In those circumstances, in the event that South Africa is, for example, knocked out of the tournament
after the Quarter Final, the Player is to notify World Rugby of her playing schedule as soon as it becomes
available so that the FPRC can confirm the fixtures to be included with the sanction.
Stephen Hardy (Chair, AU)
Foul Play Review
Stefan Terblanche (RSA)
Committee Members
Ofisa Tonu'u (NZ)
Signature Date 8 September 2025
